title: India Are In. Pakistan Might Be Out. Cricket's Olympic Return Has Already Redrawn the Map.
excerpt: The IOC has approved the qualification pathway for LA 2028 — continental representation over global rankings leaves cricket's heavyweights fighting for one wildcard spot.
body:
The last time cricket was an Olympic sport, Queen Victoria was alive. That changes in two years.

The International Olympic Committee has approved the qualification pathway for cricket at the 2028 Los Angeles Games, confirming the sport's return after a 128-year absence. Both men's and women's T20 competitions will feature six teams each — and the way those teams are chosen is already sparking controversy.

## How the Qualification Works

The system is built on continental representation, not global rankings. The top-ranked T20I team from each of four continents — Asia, Oceania, Europe, and Africa — earns a direct berth, based on ICC rankings as of December 31, 2026. The host nation, the United States, qualifies automatically from the Americas, provided it remains inside the top 15.

As things stand, the men's picture is straightforward: India from Asia, Australia from Oceania, Great Britain from Europe (using England's ranking), and South Africa from Africa. The USA men, currently 13th in the T20I rankings, are safely inside the host qualification window.

The sixth and final spot will go to the winner of the ICC Olympics Qualifier 2027, a tournament featuring the top eight unqualified sides.

## Who's Left Out — and Why They're Angry

The system's most striking casualty is Pakistan. Despite being one of cricket's most decorated and passionate nations, Pakistan are locked out by India's continental claim from Asia. New Zealand face a similar predicament behind Australia in Oceania.

Both boards are reported to be unhappy with the decision, finalized at the ICC's Annual General Meeting. For Pakistan, the sting is sharp — they will have to fight through the eight-team qualifier, a tournament where a single bad day can end everything, for a sport returning to the Olympics for the first time since the 1900 Paris Games.

The West Indies face a unique complication: the IOC does not recognize them as a single national entity. If they make the eight-team global qualifier, a separate Caribbean qualifier will first determine which individual nation represents the region.

## Women's Cricket: India Qualify, USA Miss Out

The women's pathway works differently. Qualification is based on performance at the ongoing T20 World Cup in England, and four teams have already secured their spots: Australia, South Africa, Great Britain, and India.

India Women qualified from Asia despite their semifinal exit at this week's World Cup, where Australia overpowered them. The final — England versus Australia at Lord's on Sunday — will decide the last two Olympic berths from the tournament.

The US women's team has been excluded entirely. Neither the United States nor any team from the Americas features in the ICC's top 15 women's T20I rankings, meaning the host nation will field a men's team but not a women's team at their own Games.

## For the Diaspora, This Is Personal

The tournament will be played at the Knight Riders Cricket Ground in Pomona, California — the $21 million permanent stadium being built by Shah Rukh Khan's Knight Riders Group in partnership with the Fairplex. The same venue will serve as the home of Major League Cricket's Los Angeles Knight Riders.

For the estimated 600,000 Indians and people of Indian origin living in the greater Los Angeles area, this is cricket at their doorstep. No more watching from time zones away — this is live, in person, in the summer of 2028. The scheduling has been designed with that in mind: matches will start at 9 AM and 6:30 PM Pacific time, which translates to 9:30 PM and 7:00 AM in India — prime time and morning slots.

The BCCI's backing of the Olympic bid represents a historic shift. India's board had long opposed Olympic inclusion for commercial and administrative reasons, but under Jay Shah's leadership, the board endorsed the ICC's plan. The result: India, cricket's financial superpower, will compete under the Olympic flag for the first time.

## Why It Matters Beyond Cricket

Cricket at the Olympics is more than a scheduling novelty. It places the sport inside the world's biggest multi-sport event, with the potential to reach audiences who have never watched a ball bowled. For a game that has struggled to grow beyond its traditional markets — despite the IPL's global commercial reach — Los Angeles 2028 could be a watershed.

Six teams, two groups, T20 format, 15-player squads. The structure is compact, built for television, and designed to showcase cricket's most electric format to a global audience.

For NRIs planning their 2028 summers, the message is clear: block off late July. India will be playing cricket in LA. And if Pomona tickets sell as fast as they should, the watch parties from Artesia to Edison will be the next best thing.

*Sources: Reuters, Wisden, Sporting News, IOC, ICC, Wikipedia*
